title: NRI Seafarers Can Use Contract or Discharge Certificate to Open NPS Accounts
excerpt: A PFRDA circular effective November 13 lets NRI seafarers opening an NPS Tier I account use an employment contract or a Continuous Discharge Certificate as proof of address, instead of overseas address proof.
body:
• The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) has relaxed proof-of-address rules for NRI subscribers with a seafarer work profile who are opening an NPS Tier I account.
  • Under Circular No. PFRDA/2026/55/REG-POP/10, dated November 13, 2026 and effective from that date, regulated entities must accept either a valid employment contract or a Continuous Discharge Certificate as proof of address.
  • A discharge certificate counts only if its disembarkation stamp or record is not more than six months old; an employment contract counts for a seafarer proceeding on a fresh contract.
  • This is an address-proof relaxation only: identity checks and other customer due diligence still apply in full.

NRI seafarers opening a National Pension System (NPS) Tier I account no longer have to produce conventional overseas address proof. In a circular dated November 13, 2026, the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) directed all Points of Presence, Central Recordkeeping Agencies, the NPS Trust and other stakeholders to accept either of two work documents as proof of address for this group.

Who is affected

The change is narrow. It applies to an NRI subscriber with a seafarer work profile, and only when opening an NPS Tier I account. The circular does not extend the relaxation to other subscriber categories, and its operative text names NRI subscribers; it does not state that the same document option applies to OCI cardholders. Seafarers currently serving on board a ship are covered for the address they furnish: the circular allows the current address to be given as either the overseas address of the employer or the Indian address of the subscriber.

What changed, precisely

The problem, in the circular's own words, is that "NRIs, who are in 'Seafarer' profile, are finding it difficult to provide overseas address proof at the time of onboarding into NPS." The stated purpose is "to facilitate appropriate verification of the employment and non-resident status of NRI subscribers having a seafarer work profile." The full circular text is reproduced by TaxGuru.

The amendment inserts a new provision into the note to the KYC rules for NRI onboarding, building on PFRDA's circular of December 2, 2025, which itself amended the KYC/AML/CFT Master Circular of September 25, 2025. All other provisions of those circulars remain unchanged. Under the new provision, a regulated entity must accept any one of the following as proof of address: a valid employment contract with the employer or shipping company, where the seafarer is proceeding on a fresh contract; or a Continuous Discharge Certificate, provided the disembarkation stamp or record in it is not more than six months old.

Counted here: proof of address for opening a Tier I account. Not counted: proof of identity, which is unchanged, and the wider customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence checks that PFRDA's NRI onboarding framework still requires, including PAN verification and a first transaction from a KYC-complied bank account under the 2025 circular.

When it takes effect

The circular, signed by Ashish Kumar, Chief General Manager in PFRDA's Regulation Contribution Management Department (PoP), and issued under Section 14(1) of the PFRDA Act, 2013, states that it comes into effect from the date of its issuance: November 13, 2026. Outlook Money, reporting the same circular, confirms the two accepted documents, the six-month limit on the discharge certificate, and the November 13 effective date.

What to do next

If you are an NRI seafarer opening a Tier I account, take one of the two documents to your Point of Presence: your valid employment contract if you are proceeding on a fresh contract, or your Continuous Discharge Certificate. Before applying, check the disembarkation stamp or record in the certificate: if it is more than six months old, the certificate does not qualify under this provision. If you are currently on board, you may furnish either your employer's overseas address or your Indian address as your current address. Expect the remaining onboarding checks to proceed as before, and confirm the document set with your Point of Presence before submitting, since the relaxation covers address proof only.
